messages.text:
A jagged arc of midnight-dark electricity crackled to life in Bjørn Yanitor’s open palm. The air quivered with static, and each strand of black lightning carried a faint glow of violet along its edges—a sure sign that something extraordinary was at work. 

He had always possessed a deep well of raw power, but never like this. Lightning was lightning—usually brilliant white or blue. But this? This was something altogether different. It felt older, wilder, and tethered to the very shadow between worlds. A chill swept through the onlookers as the black lightning extended, coiling around Bjørn’s arm like a living serpent.  

In the silence of the moment, nature itself seemed to hold its breath. A forest wind died at the edge of the clearing. Birds fell silent. Even the night sky—black and star-flecked—didn’t seem as dark as the lightning that crackled and danced in Bjørn’s grasp. He took a steadying breath and closed his eyes, feeling the currents surge through every nerve in his body. Then, with a focused twist of his wrist, he directed the lightning forward.  

The impact was immediate: a thunderclap boomed and shook the ground, splintering a nearby tree in a shower of sparks and broken bark. The charged atmosphere crackled and popped, momentarily illuminating Bjørn’s determined face as he fought to control the immense force in his hands.  

No one around him could look away. Black lightning was a myth—a story told to caution against meddling with powers beyond comprehension. Yet there he stood, living proof of that forbidden energy. Whether this power would prove to be a curse or an instrument of heroism was something only time would reveal—but for the moment, it was clear that Bjørn Yanitor had become more than just a rumor. He had embraced the storm inside himself, and its power crackled in dark arcs at his command.
